title: Prepaid recharge plans
text: Sarovan Telecom prepaid recharges, effective 1 June 2026. All three main recharges include unlimited local and national calls and 100 SMS per day. Daily 1.5 costs ₹299 for 28 days and gives 1.5 GB of high-speed data per day. Daily 2 costs ₹349 for 28 days and gives 2 GB per day. Long 84 costs ₹859 for 84 days and gives 2 GB per day. Daily data resets at midnight, and unused daily data does not carry forward to the next day. Once the daily quota is used, speed drops to 64 kbps until midnight. Data boosters can be added at any time: ₹19 for 1 GB valid until midnight, or ₹49 for 3 GB valid for 3 days. 5G: customers on Daily 2 and Long 84 who are in a 5G area with a 5G phone get unlimited 5G data at no extra cost; on Daily 1.5, 5G usage counts against the daily quota. Stacking: a recharge made before the current plan ends is queued and starts automatically when the current plan expires; up to 3 plans can be queued. Expiry: when a plan expires, outgoing calls, SMS and data stop immediately, while incoming calls continue for 15 days. A number with no recharge for 90 days is permanently disconnected. Prepaid recharges are non-refundable once applied, except where a recharge fails to apply but the amount is debited, in which case it is reversed within 5 working days.

title: Flex 499 postpaid plan
text: Flex 499 is the entry postpaid plan from Sarovan Telecom. Monthly rental is ₹499 plus 18% GST. Each bill cycle includes 75 GB of data, unlimited local and national calls, and 100 SMS per day. Data rollover on Flex 499: unused data rolls over to the next bill cycle only. Rolled-over data is used before the new cycle's allowance, and any rolled-over data left at the end of that next cycle expires. It does not keep accumulating from month to month, and there is no rollover bank. Extra data: after the 75 GB allowance and any rollover are used, data is charged at ₹10 per GB, billed in 1 GB blocks, up to a maximum of ₹500 per bill cycle. Once ₹500 of extra data has been billed, speed is reduced to 256 kbps for the rest of the cycle at no further charge. Add-on family lines are not available on Flex 499. Your bill cycle starts on the 1st, 8th, 15th or 22nd of the month, chosen at activation. International roaming is switched on by default, as on all postpaid connections. You can move up to Flex 549 at any time; the change applies from the next bill cycle and any rolled-over data carries across.

title: Flex 549 postpaid plan
text: Flex 549 is the family-ready postpaid plan from Sarovan Telecom. Monthly rental is ₹549 plus 18% GST. Each bill cycle includes 100 GB of data, unlimited local and national calls, 100 SMS per day, and one free add-on family line that shares the main line's data. Up to 3 more add-on lines can be added at ₹199 per month each. Data rollover on Flex 549: unused data rolls over and keeps accumulating from cycle to cycle, up to a maximum rollover balance of 200 GB. Rollover data is lost only if you move to a different plan or close the connection. Extra data: after the 100 GB allowance and any rollover are used, speed is reduced to 1 Mbps for the rest of the bill cycle, with no extra charge. If you need full speed again, a 10 GB top-up costs ₹99 and lasts until the end of the cycle. Your bill cycle starts on the 1st, 8th, 15th or 22nd of the month, chosen at activation. International roaming is switched on by default, as on all postpaid connections. Moving down to Flex 499 takes effect from the next bill cycle; the accumulated rollover balance is lost, and add-on lines must be removed or moved to their own plans first.

title: International roaming and IR packs
text: International roaming for Sarovan mobile customers. Postpaid: international roaming is switched on by default on every postpaid connection, from the day of activation. You do not need to request it before travelling. Without a pack, pay-as-you-go rates apply: data ₹55 per MB, outgoing calls ₹90 per minute, incoming calls ₹45 per minute and SMS ₹25 each. To avoid these charges, buy a pack, or switch roaming off in the Sarovan app under Manage Services or by sending ROAM OFF to 54321. Bill-shock cap: when pay-as-you-go roaming charges in one bill cycle reach ₹5,000, roaming data is paused and we send an SMS; reply YES to continue. Calls are not paused. Prepaid: roaming is off by default. Activate it in the app at least 2 hours before departure; prepaid customers can use roaming only with a pack. IR packs, valid in 42 countries including the UAE, Singapore, Thailand, the UK and the USA: IR 7 days, ₹1,999: 2 GB data, 100 minutes of calls and 20 SMS, valid for 7 days. IR 30 days, ₹3,999: 6 GB data, 250 minutes of calls and 50 SMS, valid for 30 days. Pack minutes cover incoming calls, calls to India and local calls in the country you are visiting. A pack starts when you first connect to a partner network abroad, not when you buy it. When pack data runs out, data stops; a 1 GB top-up costs ₹599.

title: Porting your number to Sarovan
text: Moving your mobile number to Sarovan Telecom. Step 1: from the number you want to move, send an SMS with the word PORT followed by your 10-digit mobile number to 1900. You will receive a Unique Porting Code (UPC). Step 2: visit a Sarovan Experience Store or book doorstep SIM delivery in the app, with your UPC and your Aadhaar for e-KYC. There is no porting fee. Timeline: Sarovan completes port-in requests within 7 working days of KYC verification. This is longer than many operators because every port-in is manually checked by our fraud-prevention team before the switch is scheduled. We will send an SMS with your switch date. Until then, keep using your old SIM; it works as normal. On the switch night, service may be unavailable for up to 4 hours between 11 pm and 3 am; once your old SIM shows no network, insert the Sarovan SIM and restart the phone. Common reasons for rejection are unpaid dues with your current operator, an expired UPC, or a name mismatch between the UPC request and your KYC. If a request is rejected, generate a new UPC and apply again. Postpaid port-in customers get 50% off the first month's rental. Porting out of Sarovan is allowed once your number has been active with us for 90 days. We do not charge for porting out, but postpaid dues must be cleared first.

title: Lost SIM, replacement SIM and eSIM
text: Lost, stolen or damaged SIM. If your phone or SIM is lost or stolen, block your number immediately in the Sarovan app or by calling 1800 210 4455 from any phone, so the number cannot be misused. Replacement SIMs are issued only at Sarovan-owned stores (Sarovan Experience Stores), not at franchise retailers or mobile shops that sell our recharges. The connection holder must come in person with original ID. If the number is registered to a family member, that person must visit; for company connections, an authorisation letter on company letterhead is needed. Charge: ₹50 for a replacement physical SIM. It is free if the SIM developed a fault within 6 months of issue. eSIM: postpaid customers can convert to eSIM in the app at no charge; prepaid customers must visit a Sarovan Experience Store. eSIM works on most recent phones; check the compatibility list in the app. Security hold: after any SIM replacement or eSIM conversion, incoming and outgoing SMS, including OTPs, are blocked for 24 hours. Calls and data start working within 2 hours of activation. Your number, plan, balance and rollover data are not affected by a SIM replacement.

title: Documents for a new connection (KYC)
text: Documents needed for a new Sarovan connection. Indian citizens, prepaid or postpaid: Aadhaar biometric e-KYC is enough on its own. No photocopies or photographs are needed, and activation usually takes about 30 minutes. Without Aadhaar: bring your original passport, voter ID or driving licence plus one passport-size photograph. Activation takes up to 24 hours after document verification. For postpaid connections taken without Aadhaar e-KYC, a refundable security deposit of ₹500 is collected. Outstation customers, whose ID address is in a different state from where the connection is bought, must also give a local address and a local reference whose number will receive a verification call. Foreign nationals: original passport with a valid visa, proof of local address in India, and a local reference. Foreign nationals can take prepaid connections only, and the connection is valid until the visa expiry date. Minors under 18 cannot hold a connection in their own name; a parent can take the connection and register the minor as the user. Business connections need the company's GST certificate, an authorisation letter and the authorised signatory's Aadhaar e-KYC. The name on bills and all communication will match the KYC document exactly.

title: Home Fibre plans
text: Sarovan Home Fibre plans. Prices are monthly rentals plus 18% GST. Fibre 100: ₹699 per month, 100 Mbps download and upload, fair usage limit of 3,300 GB per bill cycle, after which speed drops to 10 Mbps. Fibre 300: ₹999 per month, 300 Mbps, fair usage limit of 3,300 GB, then 20 Mbps. Fibre 1G: ₹3,999 per month, 1 Gbps, fair usage limit of 5,000 GB, then 50 Mbps. After crossing the fair usage limit, full speed returns automatically at the start of the next bill cycle, or immediately with a ₹199 top-up that adds 500 GB. All plans include a landline number with unlimited local and national calls through the router's phone port; you need a regular landline handset. Speeds are the maximum line speed to the router; Wi-Fi speeds on your devices depend on the device and its distance from the router. Advance rental: pay 6 months in advance for 5% off, or 12 months in advance for 10% off. Plan upgrades take effect within 4 hours; downgrades apply from the next bill cycle. Fibre 300 and Fibre 1G include a basic video streaming bundle at no extra cost.

title: Home Fibre installation, commitment and relocation
text: Installing Sarovan Home Fibre. After you book, a technician visits within 48 hours if your building is already connected. New buildings may need a feasibility survey of up to 7 working days. The one-time installation fee of ₹1,000 covers a dual-band Wi-Fi 6 router, which is yours to keep, and up to 30 metres of fibre cable inside your premises; extra cable costs ₹20 per metre. Waiver: the ₹1,000 installation fee is waived if you pay 6 or 12 months of rental in advance, or if you choose monthly billing with a 12-month commitment. Leaving early: if you close a connection on a 12-month commitment before 12 months, the waived ₹1,000 installation fee is added to your final bill. There is no other exit fee on Home Fibre. Unused full months on advance rental plans are refunded on closure. Relocation: moving within the same city costs ₹500 and is completed within 5 working days of your request, if the new address is serviceable. If the new address is not serviceable, you can close the connection without the installation fee being recovered, even within a 12-month commitment. Moving to another city is handled as a closure followed by a new connection, and the commitment carries over without charge.

title: Router warranty and technician visits
text: Your Home Fibre router and technician visits. The Wi-Fi router supplied at installation belongs to you and comes with a 12-month warranty from the installation date. Hardware faults within the warranty are fixed with a free replacement, usually within 2 working days. After the warranty, a replacement router from Sarovan costs ₹1,200, or you can use your own compatible router and we will set it up remotely at no charge. The warranty does not cover physical damage, liquid damage or damage from power surges and lightning. Before booking a visit: switch the router off for 30 seconds and back on, check that the thin fibre cable is not bent or pinched, and look at the LOS light. A red LOS light means the fibre signal is not reaching your router, so restarting will not help; please report it. Technician visits for faults in our network, or in our fibre line up to the router, are free. If the technician finds the problem is in your own devices, your internal LAN wiring, a third-party extender or Wi-Fi settings you have changed, a ₹300 visit charge is added to your next bill. The technician will tell you before starting work if the charge applies. Visit slots run from 9 am to 7 pm, seven days a week.

title: Home Fibre outage credit
text: Outage credit for Sarovan Home Fibre. If your Home Fibre service is completely down because of a fault in our network or our fibre line, you receive an automatic credit of ₹30 per full day of outage beyond the first 48 hours. The outage is counted from when the fault is logged, either by you or by our network monitoring, until service is restored. You do not need to apply: the credit appears on your next bill. The credit is capped at ₹600 per bill cycle. Example: an outage lasting 4 full days earns 2 days of credit, which is ₹60. The credit does not apply to faults in your own devices or wiring, power cuts at your premises, planned maintenance announced by SMS at least 24 hours in advance, or damage from floods, fires and other natural disasters. Repair targets: we aim to fix 90% of faults within 24 hours. Fibre cable cuts take longer, because the break has to be located and every fibre spliced, and are usually repaired within 48 hours. Mobile network outages are not covered by this credit; if you lost mobile service, contact us and we will review your case.

title: Late payment policy, effective 1 April 2024
text: Postpaid late payment and reconnection policy, effective 1 April 2024. This applies to Sarovan postpaid mobile and Home Fibre bills. Your bill is due 15 days after the bill date. A grace period of 7 days applies after the due date. If the full amount is still unpaid when the grace period ends, a late payment fee of ₹100 is added to your next bill. Barring: outgoing calls, SMS and data are barred 15 days after the due date; incoming calls continue for mobile connections. Disconnection: the connection is fully disconnected 45 days after the due date. Reconnection: a reconnection fee of ₹100 is charged whenever services are restored after barring or disconnection. Services are restored within 24 hours of payment being received. Payments made by UPI or in the app reflect within 4 hours; cheques take up to 3 working days. Autopay customers are not charged a late fee if autopay fails because of a technical error at our end. Customers facing difficulty can request a one-time extension of 10 days by calling customer care before the due date.

title: Late payment policy, effective 1 July 2026
text: Postpaid late payment and reconnection policy, effective 1 July 2026. This replaces the April 2024 version. It applies to Sarovan postpaid mobile and Home Fibre bills. Your bill is due 15 days after the bill date. There is no grace period: if the full amount has not been received by the due date, a late payment fee of ₹250 is added on the day after the due date. Partial payments do not avoid the fee. Barring: outgoing calls, SMS and data are barred 10 days after the due date; incoming calls continue for mobile connections. Disconnection: the connection is fully disconnected 30 days after the due date. Reconnection while barred: there is no reconnection fee. Pay the full outstanding amount, including any late fee, and services are restored within 2 hours. Reconnection after full disconnection: a reconnection fee of ₹200 applies, and your number is held for 60 days after disconnection. Payments made by UPI or in the app reflect within 2 hours; cheques take up to 3 working days, so pay early if you use a cheque. Autopay customers are not charged a late fee if autopay fails because of a technical error at our end. The one-time 10-day extension offered under the earlier policy has been withdrawn.

title: Closing a postpaid or Home Fibre connection
text: Closing a Sarovan postpaid mobile or Home Fibre connection. You can request closure in the Sarovan app, at any Sarovan Experience Store, or by calling 1800 210 4455. Closure takes effect within 3 working days of the request. If you want to keep your mobile number, port it out instead of closing; closing a mobile connection releases the number. Final bill: your final bill covers usage and pro-rated rental from your last bill date up to the closure date, plus any one-time charges such as a recovered installation fee. Security deposit: any security deposit is refunded within 45 days of the final bill being paid. Refunds are made only to your registered bank account, verified through a cancelled cheque or UPI; there are no cash refunds at stores. Any credit balance on your account is refunded the same way and within the same period. Routers do not need to be returned, as the router belongs to you. Prepaid connections have no closure process or fee; simply stop recharging, and the unused part of a recharge is not refundable. If you close a connection by mistake, it can be restored within 7 days at no cost, after which a fresh connection is needed.

title: Stores, customer care and complaint escalation
text: Sarovan Experience Stores are open Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 8:30 pm, and Sunday 11 am to 6 pm. They are closed on 26 January, 15 August and 2 October. Store counters in shopping malls follow the mall's opening hours. Customer care: dial 199 from a Sarovan mobile, or 1800 210 4455 from any phone. Postpaid and Home Fibre support runs 24 hours; prepaid support runs 8 am to 10 pm. Complaints: call 198 from a Sarovan mobile, or use Help in the app. Every complaint gets a docket number by SMS, and billing complaints are usually resolved within 4 working days. Escalation: if your complaint is not resolved within 7 days, or you are unhappy with the resolution, you can file an appeal with the Sarovan Appellate Authority, using the appeal form in the app or at any Sarovan Experience Store. Appeals must be filed within 30 days, and you should quote your docket number. Appeals are acknowledged within 3 days and decided within 30 days. If the outcome still does not resolve your issue, you can approach a consumer forum or the telecom regulator's complaint portal.
